main_sand_outer.bias_notes: Left-handed (Anti-clockwise). A deep, coarse sand surface that demands high baseline stamina. On dry days (moisture < 6%), the sand is deep and tiring, allowing strong stamina closers ('P' and 'S') to make ground in the 400m home straight. When moisture exceeds 10-15% (muddy/sealed), the surface packs tight and creates an extreme on-pace 'Golden Rail' speed bias.
main_sand_outer.post_bias: In 1200m and 1400m sprints, middle barriers (4–8) offer the best angle. In 1700m and 1800m route races, inside draws (1–4) hold a significant advantage by saving ground into the tight first turn.

inner_sand.bias_notes: Left-handed (Anti-clockwise) inner sand track. Features tighter turns and a shorter 350m straight. Strongly favors early gate speed ('E') and box-seat stalkers ('P'). Deep closers struggle unless a frantic pace duel unfolds.
inner_sand.post_bias: Inside barriers (1–4) are highly advantageous in 1000m, 1300m, and 1600m inner-track events. Wide barriers (8+) risk being hung wide on the turns.

handicapping_angles.moisture_content_bias_flip: Always check official KRA track moisture percentage. Moisture below 6% = heavy, deep sand (upgrade stamina & closers). Moisture above 10% = hard, fast sand (aggressively upgrade front-runners and inside gates).
handicapping_angles.kra_class_hierarchy: Korean racing uses strict Class 1 (Elite) down to Class 6 (Maiden). Pay close attention to horses moving up or down in Class. Class-dropping runners exiting Class 2 or 3 carry a distinct class advantage.
handicapping_angles.weight_handicap_impact: In KRA Class 2-5 rating handicaps, top weights carrying 57kg+ face a strict penalty against light-weight runners (52kg-54kg). Grant a significant boost to fit horses carrying low weight.
handicapping_angles.imported_vs_domestically_bred: Imported horses (USA, AUS, NZ) debuting or racing in Class 3/4 generally possess superior early gate speed and higher baseline ratings compared to local KOR-bred horses.
handicapping_angles.jockey_colony_intent: Top KRA jockeys (e.g., Antonio Davielson, CC Wong, Lim Gi-won, Moon Se-young) ride with high tactical aggression. Upgrade horses when these premier riders take the mount.
handicapping_angles.korea_cup_and_sprint_international: During the International Korea Cup ($1.6M+) & Korea Sprint ($1.4M+) in September, track class elevates to International Group 3 tier (+5.0 speed par offset).
